title: Are exponential parametrizations bijective for unrestricted module functors?
as_he_states: Are u↦e_bar(u) and u↦e(u) still bijections for arbitrary semilinear module-valued functors?
plausible_today: Both statements need substantial restrictions: formal injectivity fails for A↦A_red; ordinary parametrization requires local nilpotence even for a quasi-coherent infinite module.
state_of_art: C-SA23-misc-019 gives two exact counterexamples. On A_red, the different natural endomorphisms0,id have the same formal exponential because every nilpotent scalar acts by0. On Q[x], translations arise from d/dx, which is locally but not uniformly nilpotent. Milne2017 Theorem4.8 supplies local finite-dimensionality over a field; DuboulozLiendo2014 gives the affine Ga/LND correspondence and its carefully qualified semi-affine extension. QiaochuYuan2017 explicitly proves the module-functor classification over arbitrary Q-algebras and distinguishes local from uniform nilpotence.
why_open: The sheets ask the question without a later resolution. Their silence gives no evidence about why work stopped.
worth: A useful future task is to identify an exact class of functors where nilpotent tests detect endomorphisms; the literal question is already answered negatively.

title: The stabilizer of a graph embedding from outer fundamental-group maps
as_he_states: Does agreement of the induced outer π1 maps on every graph component imply h lies in the embedding-isotopy stabilizer H?
plausible_today: Yes for a finite graph in the interior of a compact oriented surface, with h orientation preserving. Equality of the outer maps is equivalent to homotopy on each component, and oriented homeomorphic congruence is already supplied by h.
state_of_art: C-SA23-misc-069 matches ColinMesmay2014 arXiv-version Theorem14 exactly: oriented congruence and homotopy of a finite test family of cycles give a pointwise ambient isotopy. That paper explicitly attributes the characterization to Ladegaillerie1984 and re-proves it with a linear-complexity cycle family. Esquisse1997 §3 pp13–14 directly associates Grothendieck’s question with Ladegaillerie’s1974–76 work; publication was1984. The original1984 text was not opened; the exact theorem is checked through the later full proof.

worth: The priority is historical and expository reconstruction of a resolved question, with the finite cycle test making a good computational companion.
